items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: He was down here when Louis Armstrong came to me on you somewhere in the 30 and played somewhere out there in the middle.

ctx.x: I took a fellow named Mike, he was a very versatile man like me. He played guitar in bands and sang, and he was older than me. He was down here when Louis Armstrong came to me on you somewhere in the 30 and played somewhere out there in the middle.
And you were playing banjo at this time?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: I remember Lewis's recording he would put out there, I think, in the 20s, I remember, Gipper Mouth and Gut Bucket Blues because we're all the musicians used to follow his records, you know.

ctx.x: That was the first time you see him.

I've seen him to myself. I'd heard about him around the hill, you know, but I don't remember, I remember seeing Lewis back then in the way it was from 1916 where he'd be playing in parades and things, you know. Mm-hmm. And when he went away on the boat with Faith Marble, St. Louis and things. Mm-hmm. And when he started recording, I remember Lewis's recording he would put out there, I think, in the 20s, I remember, Gipper Mouth and Gut Bucket Blues because we're all the musicians used to follow his records, you…
Well, what kind of numbers did you play with his Pierron bands, you know, what?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Lee was telling me, man, this is my good time to get to meet my good buddy Lewis

ctx.x: Is that Edna? No, not Edna.

No, not Edna. Willamina something. Willamina Borg. Yeah, Willamina Borg, yeah, yeah. So, uh, Danny was working up there and he hadn't so long, hadn't too long got married. And, uh, like he got married working on that job, yeah. So, he was good friends with Lee and also I was good friends with Danny, you know. So, they had a trip, this fella Sherman Cooks had a trip to, had an excursion trip to go to Chicago, you see. And, uh, Lewis Armstrong at the time was living in Chicago, you see. And, uh, Lee was telling me,…
You never did join the WPA band then?
